item.title: Igando accident: Woman killed as Lexus rams into commercial bus
item.description: …LASEMA responds to three emergencies across Lagos, rescues stranded motorists By Matthew Johnson A woman has been killed after a Lexus car rammed into a commercial minibus at Igando, Lagos State, in an accident that also left the bus driver injured. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) disclosed this while reporting its response to three separate emergencies across the state. The fatal accident occurred in the early hours of Friday, November 13, 2026, around Ajay Hotel, Igando, involving a Lexus car, a commercial minibus popularly known as Korope, and a pedestrian. According to preliminary information released by LASEMA, the Lexus car, which was reportedly fleeing, rammed into the minibus with registration number SMK 514 YG, causing the vehicle to strike the woman. The woman died in the incident, while the minibus driver sustained injuries and was taken to hospital before the arrival of the agency’s response team. Her remains were subsequently handed over to her relatives by officers of the Nigeria Police Force, Igando Division, in accordance with established procedures. LASEMA said its Dolphin Team, stationed in Igando, was immediately deployed after receiving a distress call and arrived at the scene within minutes. The agency, working alongside the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the police, secured the accident scene, managed traffic and coordinated the removal of the affected vehicle. The minibus was recovered and towed to the Igando Police Station with the assistance of a private tow truck, while normal traffic flow was restored. In a statement signed by LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, the state government expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured driver a speedy recovery. Oke-Osanyintolu also disclosed that the agency attended to two other emergencies within the same operational period. At Ketu-Epe Road, LASEMA concluded its follow-up response to an earlier accident involving a white minibus that plunged into a ditch. Police officers at the scene confirmed that the driver and three passengers were receiving treatment at Ketu General Hospital. The permanent secretary said the vehicle was not obstructing traffic and that the incident had been formally handed over to the police at Ketu Division for further action. In another operation, LASEMA’s Lion Squad responded to a broken-down trailer conveying a 40-foot container along Imota Road, inward Ikorodu, around Agbowa. The trailer had developed a mechanical fault, obstructing a substantial portion of the road and posing a potential danger to other motorists. No casualty was recorded in the incident, as the response team worked to ensure that the obstruction was cleared and the mechanical fault addressed. item.title: Kano drug war: PCN denies shielding illicit drug dealers
item.description: …says 1,631 drug outlets sealed in 2026, challenges task force chairman to provide evidence of alleged staff involvement By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) has denied allegations that it is shielding illicit drug dealers and facilitating the distribution of controlled substances in Kano State, insisting that it remains committed to enforcing pharmaceutical regulations. The council described the allegations by the Chairman of the Kano State Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, Muhuyi Magaji Rimin-Gado, as baseless and misleading, challenging him to provide verifiable evidence to substantiate his claims. In a rebuttal issued on Saturday and signed by Pharm. Hasiya Ladan, Consultant Pharmacist at the PCN Kano State Office, on behalf of the Registrar and Chief Executive Officer, the council disclosed that it sealed 1,631 pharmaceutical premises in Kano State in 2026 following inspections of 2,304 drug outlets. It also said 15 investigations into suspected regulatory violations were ongoing in the state, while its national enforcement team had visited Kano twice this year, in April and September. The rebuttal followed allegations made by Rimin-Gado at a press conference in Kano on November 14, where he accused the PCN and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) of allegedly protecting drug dealers operating in the state. The task force chairman had, among other things, questioned the circumstances surrounding the issuance of import licences to pharmaceutical companies dealing in pregabalin, particularly after NAFDAC rescheduled the drug as a controlled substance on September 14, 2026. He also accused the PCN of registering a pharmaceutical outlet at No. 10 Apple Avenue, allegedly located in a residential area, which he claimed was being used as a concealed distribution point for the drug. Rimin-Gado further alleged that some PCN officials were involved in clandestine drug businesses and questioned the council’s capacity to effectively regulate pharmaceutical activities in Kano, citing its relatively small number of personnel in the state. However, the PCN maintained that the regulation of pharmaceutical premises was a statutory federal responsibility backed by the Constitution, legislation and judicial pronouncements. It cited Item 21 of Part I of the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, arguing that drugs and poisons fall under the Exclusive Legislative List and that their regulation is therefore the responsibility of the Federal Government through authorised agencies. The council also referenced the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Act 2022, the Supreme Court judgment in Pharmacists Board of Nigeria v. Franklin Adegbesote (1986), and a February 16, 2024 judgment of the Federal High Court, Kano, as legal authorities affirming its regulatory mandate. item.title: When grandpas, grandmas become cocaine smugglers
item.description: …404 ‘arrested’ in 20 months By Nnamdi Ojiego The image of an elderly grandmother or grandfather being led away by anti-narcotics officers over alleged involvement in drug trafficking is one that challenges conventional perceptions of who participates in the illicit drug trade. Yet, a succession of arrests involving people in their 60s, 70s and even older has brought an uncomfortable question to the fore: Why are people who should ordinarily be enjoying their retirement years becoming involved in the dangerous business of transporting, storing and distributing illicit drugs? In Nigeria, the figures supplied by Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) suggest that the phenomenon deserves closer attention. The agency arrested 240 persons aged 60 and above for drug-related offences in 2025, comprising 191 men and 49 women. Between January and August 2026, another 164 elderly suspects, including 128 men and 36 women, were arrested. The figures bring the total number of elderly persons arrested within the 20-month period to 404. Men accounted for the overwhelming majority, representing approximately 80 per cent of the arrests in 2025 and 78 per cent in the first eight months of 2026. Calculated strategy Although the 2026 figures cover only eight months and cannot be directly compared with the full-year 2025 total, the number of arrests already recorded points to the continued involvement of older people in drug-related activities. It also raises questions about the circumstances drawing them into a trade whose consequences include lengthy imprisonment, financial ruin, damaged family relationships and, in some cases, serious health risks. The NDLEA also reported seizing 6,998.77 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in connection with elderly suspects in 2025, compared with 1,479.988 kilogrammes between January and August 2026. From couriers to local dealers The cases recorded by the NDLEA in 2026 provide a glimpse into the different ways older people are becoming involved in the illicit drug trade. On March 14, 2026, NDLEA operatives arrested 74-year-old Ikwuakalom Nwakoro Emeka at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, while he was preparing to board a British Airways flight to London. The agency alleged that 11 kilogrammes of cocaine were discovered in his luggage, concealed in food items, including ground dry pepper. He reportedly told investigators he was travelling to Britain on holiday. Barely three months later, another high-profile case emerged at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos. On June 28, operatives arrested 67-year-old Mary Yetunde Barek, a Nigerian-British woman who worked as a caregiver in the United Kingdom, while she was preparing to board a Virgin Atlantic flight to London. The NDLEA alleged that 13 kilogrammes of cocaine were recovered from 31 large packages concealed in plantain peels designed to resemble actual plantain hands and packed among other food items. item.title: 60 DAYS TO POLLS: Fear over electoral process as political attacks rise
item.description: …Report says 640 killed in October as a result of broader insecurity …Experts warn against violence, fake news By Nnamdi Ojiego 60 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns are mounting over the safety of the electoral process as rising insecurity, attacks on political gatherings and the spread of misinformation threaten to undermine citizens’ participation in the polls. The concerns have been heightened by fresh incidents of political violence in different parts of the country, including Calabar, Cross River State, Asaba, Delta State, and Sokoto, where political supporters and opposition figures have reportedly come under attack. The developments have renewed questions about the preparedness of security agencies to protect candidates, party supporters and voters, particularly in a country already grappling with banditry, insurgency, kidnapping and communal violence. A report by the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD), Nigeria Election Security Tracker for October 2026 provides a troubling picture of the security situation. It recorded 640 deaths during the month (October), representing a 61.62 per cent increase from the 396 deaths recorded in September. Of the 640 deaths, 638 were attributed to broader insecurity, while two resulted from election-related attacks in Enugu and Ebonyi. The North-East accounted for the highest number of fatalities, with 409 deaths. The report also documented 16 election-related incidents in October, compared with 14 in September, representing a 14.29 per cent increase. Attacks on campaign gatherings and convoys accounted for 11 of the 16 incidents. Other cases involved assaults on individuals, attacks on political property and the restriction of a political gathering. The incidents affected several political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC) and African Democratic Congress (ADC), which each recorded four cases, while the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) recorded three. Two of the incidents were fatal. Ifeanyi Nwolie died from gunshot injuries sustained during the NDC campaign launch in Enugu on October 10. In Ebonyi, gunmen attacked the convoy of NDC candidate, Rollins Offia-Nwali, on October 22, killing one person, injuring three others and burning his vehicle. The candidate reportedly escaped. The CDD report also documented attacks on ADC convoys in Igueben and Kogi, disruption of PDP consultations in Calabar, an attack on an ADC candidate’s meeting in Obosi, Anambra State, and the prevention of supporters from gathering for the Obi-Kwankwaso march in Abuja. Although broader insecurity accounted for most of the fatalities, the report warned that its consequences could extend to the electoral process, particularly in communities where residents have been displaced or roads have become unsafe. item.title: Christian persecution in Nigeria worrisome — Catholic bishops
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. In his address, Archbishop Ugorji said the human and material consequences of the country’s insecurity remained alarming, irrespective of whether the crisis was viewed as targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict. “Ultimately, whether the crisis is perceived as a targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict, the human and material toll is undeniable. “It is deeply troubling that tens of thousands have lost their lives, millions remain internally displaced, the education of thousands of children is truncated, and millions of naira have been lost through destruction of property and paying ransom,” he said. item.title: Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.” On security in the state, Governor Okpebholo said his administration took stiff measures to reduce the level of killings and kidnapping in the state. Some of the measures, he said, was destroying any building that was linked to kidnapping and cult related activities in the state irrespective of the social status of the person involved. He said: “These are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us. To be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights. Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night. “In the next few weeks, it will be safer because there will be police at every corner of the state to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. Whether you take a bush path, they will follow you up.” The post Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Yari to critics: You did nothing about insecurity for 20 yrs
item.description: …Says, FAAC allocations now in trillions By Omeiza Ajayi The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has told those saying the party has no plan for security that they did nothing about insecurity in 20 years. He spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Jos, the Plateau State capital. “Those who are saying we don’t have plan for security, I want to remind them that they did nothing about insecurity for over 20 years about it because it started during their time,” Yari said. According to him, the APC will implement its manifesto to the letter, promising that by 2031 almost everything promised would have been achieved. Yari told the gathering that Plateau’s political players had come out to assure the President of the state’s votes in the 2027 general election. “The key players, active players in the Plateau politics are all here before you to give you the assurances that 2027 Plateau is 101% assured,” he said. He described Tinubu as “the person that met the federation account of Nigeria as at June 2023 at N732 billion. But today, we thank God, Mr President, we thank you for your hard work and your special leadership. We are now counting the federation account in trillions.” The post Yari to critics: You did nothing about insecurity for 20 yrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Tinubu Northern Youth Forum has announced its decision to withdraw support for President Bola Tinubu and back former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The group also announced a change of identity, adopting the name Arewa Youth For Atiku (AYA) as part of its new political direction. The decision was contained in a statement signed by Adamu Jikan Manu on behalf of the group on November 13, 2026. According to the statement, the formal endorsement of Atiku, declaration of support and official defection to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) will take place on Saturday, November 14, at the party’s North-East Strategic Office in Azare, Bauchi State. The ceremony will be led by the group’s Convener, Hon. Auwal Ibrahim Sansani, CNA. The group said its transition from Tinubu Northern Youth Forum to Arewa Youth For Atiku was intended to provide a broader platform for youth engagement, political awareness, community outreach and participation in the democratic process across Northern Nigeria. It called on its members, supporters, community and religious leaders, youth and women organisations, students, market associations, professionals and other stakeholders to attend the declaration ceremony. The statement said the group believed Nigeria needed responsible leadership, national unity, effective governance and meaningful citizens’ participation. It also urged Nigerians who shared its vision to join its campaign for peaceful and democratic participation ahead of the 2027 general election. The group concluded its statement with the slogan: “Join the Atiku Train. Vote Atiku, Save Nigeria.” The post Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Keyamo: No one sings ‘On Your Mandate’ in place of anthem, accuses NDC of secessionism
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has defended the use of the campaign song, On Your Mandate, to welcome President Bola Tinubu at public events, insisting that it is never sung in place of Nigeria’s national anthem. Keyamo also accused the National Democratic Congress (NDC) of promoting secessionism, alleging that singing an outlawed national anthem in place of the legally recognised anthem amounted to an expression of a desire to have a separate country. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Sunday while responding to what he described as attempts by some individuals to equate the use of Tinubu’s campaign song with the singing of the former national anthem. The minister explained that supporters of Tinubu always observe the national anthem at official events before singing On Your Mandate to celebrate the President. “At no time have supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sung ON YOUR MANDATE IN PLACE of the National Anthem. At every occasion, the NATIONAL ANTHEM is always sung as a mark of recognition of one of our most important national symbols, and then the President is serenaded by his supporters with ON YOUR MANDATE,” he said. Keyamo maintained that nobody should prevent the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, from adopting a song, including the former national anthem, as his campaign or personal song. He, however, insisted that such a song must be performed either before or after the legally recognised national anthem has been rendered. The minister also defended the Police Band’s use of the instrumental version of On Your Mandate to herald Tinubu’s arrival at public functions or his decision to address an audience. According to him, the practice is consistent with established presidential protocol, under which the Police Band plays an instrumental piece whenever the President arrives at an event or rises to speak. He cited the administrations of former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, saying the Police Band similarly played musical pieces to herald their arrival at the National Assembly or before they addressed gatherings. Keyamo said the On Your Mandate instrumental is sometimes played by the Police Band to announce Tinubu’s presence or speech, but only after the national anthem has been rendered. He further argued that the practice was not unusual, pointing out that several states in Nigeria have their own anthems, which are performed after the national anthem at official functions. The minister, however, drew a distinction between the adoption of a campaign or state anthem and the singing of an outlawed national anthem in place of the officially recognised one. item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. The post 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad. The post Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims appeared first on Channels Television .
